P1: Renamed (Jan 2026 PSA): Player:LoadCharacter -> Player:LoadCharacterAsync; BadgeService:AwardBadge -> BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync; MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync. Not renamed: Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer keep their names (as do InvokeClient / BindableFunction:Invoke). The old names still work: they are deprecated informationally only, with identical arguments and behaviour and no removal scheduled. Use the Async names in new code and wrap them in pcall, since they yield and can throw.
P2: Enable it in Workspace > Server Authority: set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (fully released July 2026). It forces NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation. Put client-predicted gameplay logic in a shared ModuleScript (required by both server and client) and register it with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn), so the client predicts it and the server re-simulates and corrects it. Inside the simulation callback, don't Destroy or reparent instances, call EquipTool, or read UserInputService. Read input from Input Action System actions instead. Use time() as the clock. Don't use tick(), os.clock() or os.time(). Expect streaming bugs (missing parts) when you turn it on in an older non-streaming game.
P3: The property is Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Timeline: Phase 1 (June 2026) defaults to Disabled and is opt-in. Phase 2 (planned early 2027) defaults to Enabled. Phase 3 (planned mid 2027) removes the property, so IAS becomes the only path. Server Authority mode already forces it on. At risk: code that calls require(PlayerModule):GetControls() or otherwise reaches into the ControlModule; code relying on the old input sinking/priority (ContextActionService binds that override movement keys, UserInputService gameProcessed assumptions); and forked or customized PlayerModule copies. Forked player scripts must set StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule appropriately (Disabled) or be migrated.
P4: It introduced platform-integrated chat, opted into with TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat = Enabled (opt-in in Studio). Under it, TextChatMessage.Text and .Translation return "" with a warning, PrefixText is unsupported, and OnIncomingMessage / Player.Chatted no longer expose message text for your own moderation or parsing. Custom chat UIs must move to the TextChannelWindow model, preset messages become Quick Words, and chat commands should use TextChatCommand. Games that parse chat text or draw their own chat bubbles and windows will break. Timeline: opt-in now until Feb 2027, default on in Feb 2027 with an opt-out (an opt-out until about March 2027 was also mentioned), and mandatory around May 2027. Don't build new features that read TextChatMessage.Text.
P5: Budgets are per experience, per minute, and shared by all servers and Open Cloud. They scale with concurrent users (CCU): Read = 300 + 40 x CCU; Write = 300 + 20 x CCU; List = 300 + 2 x CCU; Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU. (Some doc pages say 250 + CCU x ..., so design for the lower number.) Per key, throughput is about 25 MB/min read and 4 MB/min write, with each request rounded up to 1 KB. Storage limit = 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime users, measured compressed, latest versions only. UpdateAsync counts as one read plus one write, so it consumes both budgets. Over-budget requests queue (30 per type) and then fail.
P6: Gems bought with Robux count as a Robux-purchasable currency, so crates bought with Gems are paid random items, and so is anything that indirectly costs Robux. Before purchase, show the odds of every possible item as numeric percentages that sum to 100%, behind a clearly labelled Info or Details button (a bare (i) icon isn't enough). The Luck Potion changes the odds, so you must explain numerically how it changes them before purchase, and the displayed odds must update while the boost is active. Per player, call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync on the server. If ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted is true, don't sell random crates for paid currency: hide or block them, or offer a free or direct-purchase alternative. If IsPaidItemTradingAllowed is false, block trading of paid items. Fail closed: if the lookup fails, treat the player as restricted. Re-check on the server in the purchase and receipt handlers, not only in the UI.

Daily Engagement pays 5 Robux per qualifying Active Spender per day (they play 10+ minutes, and it counts among the first few experiences they play that day). Audience Expansion pays 35% of a new or returning (reactivated) user's spending in their first 60 days, up to the first $100, when you brought them in via share links, direct links or search. That requires an ID-verified creator. Rewards are credited as Earned Robux with a hold of about 60 days. DevEx: the standard rate is $0.0038 per Earned Robux. G1: Rules: (1) Assign ProcessReceipt exactly once, on the server. (2) Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. If the player is missing or anything fails, return NotProcessedYet, and Roblox will retry later or on rejoin. (3) Be idempotent by receiptInfo.PurchaseId: record processed PurchaseIds in the player's saved data, in the same UpdateAsync or atomic save as the grant, and if the ID is already recorded return PurchaseGranted without granting again. (4) Don't yield forever or error. pcall the DataStore calls and use UpdateAsync rather than Get-then-Set. (5) Look the product up by ProductId. Charged but nothing: the callback returned PurchaseGranted even though the save failed or the player had left, or it errored (for example, a nil player). Received twice: the callback granted, then failed before returning, or returned NotProcessedYet after granting, so Roblox retried and it granted again with no PurchaseId check. A race with a non-atomic Get+Set can also do it.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one (currency, inventory, counters), when several servers might write the same key (trading, teleports, rejoin), or for session locking and receipt deduping. It reads and writes atomically, so concurrent writes can't silently overwrite each other. SetAsync blindly overwrites. It's only acceptable for a fresh, independent value, and even then it risks clobbering newer data. Transform function rules: it must be fast and must not yield (no waits, no other DataStore calls, no remotes). It may be called multiple times, so it must be pure, with no side effects like granting items. Treat the old value as possibly nil and validate it. Return the new value, or return nil to cancel the write. Don't mutate shared state outside it. Keep the result under the 4 MB value limit. Remember that UpdateAsync costs a read plus a write, and pcall it.
G3:
No. typeof(gold) == "number" lets through NaN (NaN < 0 and NaN > x are both false), inf and -inf (inf is caught by the second check, but NaN is not), and fractional values like 0.0001. It also doesn't stop spam, and it only checks the balance when the offer is created, not when the trade completes, so a player can offer the same gold in several trades or spend it before acceptance. Fix: reject NaN with gold ~= gold, require an integer that is finite and inside a sane range, and rate-limit the remote. Then reserve or escrow the gold on the server (or re-validate and deduct atomically when the trade completes), and read the balance from server-side data rather than a value the client could influence.
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
    if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
    if gold < 1 or gold > 1e9 or gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
    if not rateLimit(player) then return end
    createOffer(player, gold) -- escrow now; re-check + deduct atomically on accept
end)
```
G4: The Animator recomputes Motor6D.Transform every frame for every joint that a playing track keys. It writes during the animation step, after Heartbeat and PreRender, so your Heartbeat write is overwritten whenever the idle track keys that joint. Write procedural offsets after the Animator has run: connect to RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after animation and before physics/render. Combine your offset with the animated value instead of replacing it: motor.Transform = aimCFrame * motor.Transform (or animated * offset, depending on the space you need). For joints no track keys, don't keep multiplying onto Transform every frame, because it compounds. Set it absolutely or reset it each frame. Alternatively, remove the barrel/yaw joints from the idle animation or play aim as a higher-priority track. Edit C0 (or C1) only for static or rarely changing rest offsets such as mount and grip positions. The Animator never overwrites C0, but changing it every frame is a replication-heavy and physics-unfriendly substitute for Transform.
G5: The Animator blends per joint. For each joint, only tracks that actually key that joint compete. The highest AnimationPriority among those tracks wins: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. A higher-priority track at weight 1 fully owns the joint. If its effective weight is below 1, the remainder goes to lower-priority tracks, so Action at 0.6 lets walk show 0.4. Tracks of equal priority blend by their relative weights: they're summed and normalised, and a total below 1 pulls toward the rest pose. Effective weight is the weight set by Play(fadeTime, weight) or AdjustWeight, multiplied by the fade-in progress. The swing looks weak because it's probably the same priority as walk (Movement or Core, often the default when authored), so the two average out. Or its weight or fade is low. Fix: set the swing track's Priority to Action (or higher) before or when playing, play it at weight 1 with a short fade, and key only the upper-body joints so the legs still walk.
G6: Blender works in metres while Roblox works in studs, and the FBX unit-scale handshake gets multiplied twice. Blender's default FBX export writes Unit Scale 1.0 = 1 cm (Apply Scalings "All Local"/"FBX Units Scale" mismatch), and Studio's importer then converts cm to studs, so a 1 m object becomes about 100 studs. Recommended: Blender Scene Units = Metric with Unit Scale 1.0 (or 0.01 per some workflows), apply rotation and scale in Blender (Ctrl+A), and export FBX with Apply Scalings = "FBX Units Scale", Scale 1.0, Forward -Z / Up Y, and Apply Unit/Transform as recommended. In Studio's 3D Importer, check the file's scale units (set Scale Unit to Studs or match) and preview before importing. Or export glTF/GLB, which has no unit ambiguity. Don't fix it by rescaling in Studio, especially rigs.
G7: Modifiers are non-destructive and live only in Blender. The exporter writes the base mesh unless it evaluates the modifiers, so with "Apply Modifiers" unchecked you get the un-mirrored half and the un-bevelled sharp edges. Fix: tick Include > Apply Modifiers in the glTF exporter (Data > Mesh > Apply Modifiers), or apply the modifiers manually (Ctrl+A) on a copy before exporting. The catch: the glTF exporter can't apply modifiers on meshes that have shape keys, so the shape keys/morph targets are dropped or the modifiers are skipped. With an armature, Apply Modifiers would also bake the Armature modifier and break skinning. So for rigged or shape-keyed meshes, apply Mirror and Bevel manually first (before adding shape keys or skinning, or via an add-on), and leave the Armature modifier live. Also make sure Bevel uses enough segments and smooth shading, so you don't get only sharp edges.
G8: (1) Scale-only size means 30% of the width by 30% of the height, so the shape follows the screen's aspect ratio and is stretched on wide or tall screens. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (for example AspectRatio = 1, or the design ratio, with DominantAxis set and AspectType = FitWithinMaxSize), or size one axis by scale and derive the other. Add UISizeConstraint or UIScale for min/max sizes. (2) The top-left corner is under the device's unsafe area (notch, rounded corners) and the Roblox top bar/menu buttons. Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = DeviceSafeInsets, or CoreUISafeInsets so it also avoids the top bar, and keep IgnoreGuiInset = false. Alternatively, offset the button by GuiService.TopbarInset (read live, don't hard-code a 36/58 px bar) and the safe-area insets. For full-bleed art, use a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None (and IgnoreGuiInset = true) at a lower DisplayOrder.

```lua
-- Server Script
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local BuyItem = RS:WaitForChild("BuyItem")
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {price=..., maxQty=...}
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
    local now = os.clock()
    if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.25 then return end
    last[player] = now
    if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
    if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity
        or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
    local item = Items[itemId]            -- server-side price, never client's
    if not item then return end
    local cost = item.price * quantity
    local data = PlayerData.get(player)   -- server-owned profile
    if not data or data.Coins < cost then return end
    data.Coins -= cost                    -- deduct and grant together
    data.Inventory[itemId] = (data.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Validate types, NaN, integers and range, use server-side prices, rate-limit, and clean up per-player state.

```lua
-- key = "u_"..userId ; value = {data=..., lock={jobId=..., t=os.time()}}
local LOCK_TTL = 90 -- renewed by every autosave (< TTL)
function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 6 do
    local ok, res = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or {data = defaults(), lock = nil}
      local l = old.lock
      if l and l.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - l.t < LOCK_TTL then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel write
      end
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and res and res.lock.jobId == game.JobId then return res.data end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- wait for other server to release
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin") -- never play on unloaded data
end
function save(player, release)
  pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end
    old.data = cache[player]
    old.lock = (not release) and {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()} or nil
    return old
  end)
end
-- autosave every ~60-120s with jitter (renews lock); PlayerRemoving -> save(p,true)
-- before TeleportAsync: save(p,true) first; BindToClose: save all in parallel, wait
-- trades/receipts: record PurchaseId/tradeId inside the same UpdateAsync
```
Never save if the load failed. Locks expire so a crashed server can't hold them forever. Or use ProfileStore, which does all of this.

T4: FireServer automatically sends the firing player as the first OnServerEvent argument. The client also passed LocalPlayer explicitly, so the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50). amount is therefore the Player Instance, and amount + 1 errors. Fix the client: remote:FireServer(50). Keep the server signature function(player, amount). Also validate it on the server: if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end. Never trust a client-sent player argument: the implicit first parameter is the only reliable identity. (FireClient(player, ...) does need the player; FireServer does not.)
T5:
In Studio solo play, the local player can join before your server Script runs and connects PlayerAdded (especially if the script yields first, for example with a require or WaitForChild before connecting). That player's PlayerAdded already fired, so the handler never runs for them. On live servers, scripts usually load before anyone joins, which hides the race. Standard fix: connect first, then loop over the players already present.
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    local ls = Instance.new("Folder"); ls.Name = "leaderstats"
    local c = Instance.new("IntValue"); c.Name = "Coins"; c.Parent = ls
    ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also make sure the folder is named exactly "leaderstats" and parented to the Player.

```lua
local BadgeService = game:GetService("BadgeService")
local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardObbyBadge(player: Player)
    -- skip if already owned
    local okHas, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
```

T8: RenderFidelity is not a runtime-scriptable property. It's baked when the MeshPart is created or imported (set it in Studio, via plugins, or in CreateMeshPartAsync options), so setting it from a game script has no effect. Also check that you actually saved and published the Studio edit. Precise does keep the mesh at full detail at any distance. Other things lower detail in a live game: (1) Model streaming LOD. With StreamingEnabled and the parent Model's LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh (or Automatic), distant or unstreamed models are drawn as low-poly imposter meshes regardless of RenderFidelity. Set Model.LevelOfDetail = Disabled (and/or ModelStreamingMode = Persistent) for hero models. (2) Client graphics quality. Low quality levels and mobile devices reduce draw distance and detail, which Studio (often at max quality) doesn't show. (3) Automatic fidelity on other parts, such as unions, accessories and textures (Automatic steps down at about 250 and 500 studs). Verify with a test place on the target device.
